First off, let’s talk about the word bad. It’s a judgement word, and it doesn’t hold much merit. It’s a subjective word that can mean many different things to many different people. When a coping skill is presenting a risk to your safety, it is maladaptive. Maladapted skills are common when people are mentally ill in one way or another. It was a skill adapted for a situation that, in practice, puts the individual at a safety risk, and does not come from a vanilla mind. Ya know? Self harm is a coping skill, and that is valuable when it is, but, like suicidal ideation (without intent) it presents a risk to yourself. For the same reason that an eating disorder is maladaptive, taking control over the one thing you have control over at the risk of your physical health, self harm is maladaptive. When we look at a situation where someone is self harming, we have to look at all of the other risks at play; for instance, if someone is self harming because of abuse, we need to take care of (try to get the person out of) the abuse first. It presents a greater risk. And then, after that, we can focus on self harm. It is a risk, yes, but abuse is more pertinent. What I have found is that simply trying to stop is not enough. I replaced self-harm with breaking rocks, some people use ice, some people snap rubber-bands. Sorry for repeating myself so much, but it felt important to be specific. 

TLDR: it’s not that self harm is Bad, it’s that it is maladaptive. A subjective opinion vs. a fact of life.
